data.topic: iterative auto-fix loop skill for Claude Code CLI

findings.summary: Ralph Loop (Step 5.0) already implements a detect-fix-revalidate loop for build errors inside run-stories
findings.details: run-stories/SKILL.md Step 5.0 ('Ralph Loop auto-review') runs build-verify.sh after each coder returns DONE, and on failure re-injects a retry agent with the build errors. It tracks retry_count, last_error_hash (SHA-256), consecutive_no_progress, and error_hash_counts. Circuit breakers: max 3 retries, 3 consecutive no-progress, 5 same-error. This is the closest existing pattern to a fix loop — but it's embedded inline in run-stories, not a standalone skill.

findings.summary: Coder escalation and restart patterns exist in merge-worktree for plan-level vs execution-level failures
findings.details: merge-worktree/SKILL.md defines two distinct recovery paths: (1) Escalation: 2 BLOCKING round-trips → Opus coder (architect only), still BLOCKING → blocked. (2) Restart: if plan was wrong (not coder incapable), reset worktree, write new plan, relaunch at same model level, max 1 restart. This restart-vs-escalation distinction maps to diagnosis: was the fix wrong, or was the plan wrong?

findings.summary: Ralph Loop plugin (installed, enabled) implements stop-hook-based session re-injection with iteration tracking
findings.details: The ralph-loop plugin at plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/ralph-loop/ uses a Stop hook to intercept session exit. State stored in .claude/ralph-loop.local.md (markdown frontmatter with iteration count, max_iterations, completion_promise, session_id). Stop hook reads transcript, checks for <promise> tags indicating completion, and re-injects the same prompt. Session-scoped via session_id. This is the canonical pattern for iterative loops in Claude Code.

findings.summary: Skills use YAML frontmatter in SKILL.md with standardized fields: name, description, args, optional disable-model-invocation
findings.details: All skills follow the same pattern: YAML frontmatter (name, description, args with name/type/description), then markdown body with numbered steps. Only prefs/SKILL.md uses disable-model-invocation: true. Skills reference each other via Skill tool invocations. Context: fork is not used by any existing skill.

findings.summary: Build verification uses a shared script (build-verify.sh) returning structured JSON with project-type detection
findings.details: run-stories and merge-worktree both reference build-verify.sh with --project-root flag. Returns JSON with status, build_result (pass/fail/skip), project_type, build_output, lint_warnings. Project type detected from filesystem markers (package.json, pubspec.yaml, Cargo.toml, go.mod, pyproject.toml). The script is referenced but lives at ~/.claude/scripts/build-verify.sh.

findings.summary: Verify skill implements hierarchical validation: review → build → test → acceptance criteria walk
findings.details: verify/SKILL.md runs in sequence: (1) integrated review via reviewer agent on full diff, (2) build and test with project-type detection, (3) acceptance criteria walk with programmatic vs manual verification classification. This is the closest existing skill to a validation pyramid.

findings.summary: Lint skill is a standalone pre-merge check that detects linter from package.json and runs npm run lint
findings.details: lint/SKILL.md resolves worktree path, detects lint script in package.json, runs npm run lint, reports errors/warnings. It does NOT auto-fix — it reports only. A fix loop would need to wrap this detection pattern with fix attempts.

findings.summary: Subagent return contract: DONE/NEED_DECISION/BLOCKED terminal status
findings.details: ORCHESTRATION.md §15 mandates every delegated subagent returns exactly one of: DONE: <summary>, NEED_DECISION: <question>, or BLOCKED: <reason>. The main session parses only the terminal status line. A fix-loop skill must conform to this contract.

findings.summary: Main session cannot use EnterWorktree — all worktrees created by background coder agents only
findings.details: ORCHESTRATION.md §1: 'MUST NOT use EnterWorktree or git worktree add'. Exception: merge-worktree uses ephemeral /tmp/ worktrees. A fix-loop skill in the main session must operate on existing worktrees or launch coders that create them.

findings.summary: Coder agents must not call mcp__gemini__* tools — Gemini is orchestrator-only
findings.details: All coder prompts include: 'Do NOT call any mcp__gemini__* tools. Gemini is a research tool for the orchestrator — not available to coders.' A fix loop that re-injects coders inherits this constraint.

findings.summary: Model selection follows static table + trust-informed overrides (ORCHESTRATION §2)
findings.details: Coder default is Sonnet, escalation to Opus after 2 BLOCKING round-trips. Haiku only when ALL threshold criteria met (single file, exact code, no regex, no complex logic, not a pipeline file). Trust scores from merge_outcomes override when >=10 records exist.

findings.summary: Hook system supports PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionStart, SubagentStop, UserPromptSubmit
findings.details: settings.json defines hooks with matchers (Edit|Write, Bash, EnterWorktree, Read, Skill, TaskUpdate) and command scripts. Stop hooks can block session exit by returning {decision: 'block', reason: <prompt>}. The Ralph Loop plugin uses this mechanism. A fix-loop could use Stop hooks for re-injection OR could use the skill system with explicit iteration.

findings.summary: Scripts directory pattern: shared bash/python scripts in ~/.claude/scripts/ returning structured JSON
findings.details: Established pattern: scripts like build-verify.sh, diff-gate.sh, worktree-setup.sh, worktree-cleanup.sh live in ~/.claude/scripts/ and return JSON on stdout. Exit codes: 0=success, 1=functional error, 2=system error. Skills call these scripts and parse JSON results. Currently only 5 actual scripts exist (setup-memory.sh, om-cleanup.py, brainlift_pdf.py, claude-profile.sh, log-correction.sh) — the build/gate scripts are referenced but may not exist yet.

findings.summary: Ralph Loop plugin is installed and enabled globally
findings.details: plugins/installed_plugins.json shows ralph-loop@claude-plugins-official installed. settings.json has enabledPlugins: {ralph-loop@claude-plugins-official: true}. The plugin's Stop hook will fire in every session. A new fix-loop skill must coordinate with or wrap the Ralph Loop, not duplicate it.

findings.summary: No test infrastructure exists in the dotclaude orchestration project
findings.details: No package.json, no test directories under ~/.claude/, no test framework. The project is shell scripts, Python scripts, SKILL.md markdown files, and JSON configs. Testing is done via /smoke-test skill (integration testing with throwaway artifacts) rather than unit tests. The .claude/.claude/tests/ directory exists but was not explored.

findings.summary: All occurrences of fix/retry loop patterns mapped across the codebase
findings.details: Fix/retry patterns found in: (1) run-stories Step 5.0 Ralph Loop, (2) run-stories Step 5b merge gate retry (compile_error → test agent retry, logic_failure → coder retry, max 1 retry each), (3) merge-worktree escalation (2 BLOCKING → Opus) and restart (plan wrong → new plan, max 1), (4) critique SKILL.md self-critique loop (max 2 iterations + Gemini escalation), (5) Ralph Loop plugin stop hook. No other retry/fix loop patterns exist.

findings.summary: A new fix-loop skill would integrate with run-stories (Step 5.0 replacement) and ship pipeline
findings.details: The primary integration points are: (1) run-stories Step 5.0 could delegate to /fix-loop instead of inline Ralph Loop retry, (2) ship pipeline Step 5 runs run-stories which triggers Step 5.0, (3) quickfix Step 7 launches a coder that currently has no auto-fix loop, (4) merge-worktree Step 2.5 smoke test could trigger fix-loop on failure. Standalone /fix-loop invocation would be a new entry point.

decisions_relevant.summary: Agent health monitoring: dual-gate pattern detection + soft resource budget with watchdog in run-state.db
decisions_relevant.impact: Fix loop must respect the agent-watchdog.py monitoring. Re-injected fix agents should be monitored by the same watchdog, or the fix-loop needs its own iteration-level health check.

decisions_relevant.summary: Merge queue: priority queue with dependency locking, non-conflicting stories skip queue
decisions_relevant.impact: Fix loop operates within a single story's worktree — merge queue is downstream. But fix-loop must not hold up the merge queue by running indefinitely.

decisions_relevant.summary: Graduated autonomy: global trust + domain-scoped overrides from merge_outcomes
decisions_relevant.impact: Fix loop iterations could feed into trust scores. Stories that require many fix-loop iterations should reduce trust for that domain.

decisions_relevant.summary: Policy-mechanism split: extract procedural blocks to scripts, keep orchestration in SKILL.md
decisions_relevant.impact: Fix loop should follow this pattern — detection/verification scripts in scripts/, orchestration/retry logic in SKILL.md.

decisions_relevant.summary: Transient state in separate run-state.db, not epics.db
decisions_relevant.impact: Fix loop iteration state (retry counts, error hashes, progress metrics) should go to run-state.db if persisted.

decisions_relevant.summary: Visual iteration loop: 3-cycle budget with evolutionary prompt regeneration
decisions_relevant.impact: Established precedent for bounded iteration with evolution. Fix loop should use similar bounded iteration with error context injection (not just re-running the same prompt).

conflicts.subject: Stop hook vs explicit skill iteration for loop control
conflicts.codebase_says: Ralph Loop plugin uses Stop hook re-injection (decision: block + reason: prompt). This is the established pattern for iterative loops. The plugin is installed and enabled.
conflicts.research_says: Research documents both stop-hook-based (Ralph Loop) and explicit-loop patterns (Aider's --auto-test, SWE-agent's state machine). Research also notes that Claude Code skills support context: fork for isolated subagent execution.
conflicts.resolution: Codebase wins. The new fix-loop skill should either (a) extend/configure the Ralph Loop plugin for its specific use case, or (b) implement its own iteration loop inline in the skill SKILL.md using the same stop-hook pattern. Since the fix loop needs structured multi-phase validation (not just re-running one prompt), an explicit skill with per-iteration logic is likely better than pure stop-hook re-injection. The Ralph Loop handles 'keep running this prompt until done' — a fix loop needs 'run different commands at each phase'.

conflicts.subject: Unified fix loop vs embedded in run-stories
conflicts.codebase_says: Run-stories Step 5.0 has the Ralph Loop inline with circuit breakers. This handles build errors only. Step 5b handles test failures via merge gate retry (max 1 retry). These are separate mechanisms for different error types.
conflicts.research_says: Research recommends a unified detect→diagnose→fix→revalidate loop handling all error types. A hierarchical validation pyramid (syntax→lint→types→tests) is structural, not optional.
conflicts.resolution: Research wins on unification. A standalone /fix-loop skill extracts and unifies the inline retry logic from run-stories Step 5.0 and Step 5b into one reusable skill. Run-stories delegates to /fix-loop instead of inlining. This also makes the loop callable from /quickfix and standalone.

conflicts.subject: Iteration budget: 3 retries (codebase) vs 3-5 for tight loops / 10 for patch budgets (research)
conflicts.codebase_says: Run-stories Step 5.0 uses max 3 retries. Merge-worktree allows max 1 restart. Critique allows max 2 self-iterations.
conflicts.research_says: Aider uses 3 reflections, ChatRepair/ThinkRepair use 5, Art of Repair uses 10 total patches across strategies. SWE-agent recommends 50 turns with $1 cost cap.
conflicts.resolution: Codebase pattern wins for default — 3 retries per error type is consistent with established practice. But the fix loop should allow configurable --max-retries flag for callers that want more budget (e.g., standalone invocation vs embedded in run-stories).

blast_radius.failure_symptoms: If fix-loop has a bug: (1) infinite loops if circuit breakers fail, (2) stories marked DONE despite failing builds if fix-loop falsely reports success, (3) context window exhaustion if error output is not truncated, (4) merge queue stalls if fix-loop holds a story indefinitely

gaps: No established pattern for visual regression detection in the codebase — screenshot capture, comparison, and diff-to-text conversion would be entirely greenfield
No unified error normalization exists — build-verify.sh returns raw build_output, lint and test errors are project-type-specific strings, no structured error schema
No pattern for runtime error detection (catching errors from a running dev server or app) — all existing validation is build-time or test-time
No counterexample injection pattern exists — failed patches are not tracked as negative examples for subsequent fix attempts
No adaptive convergence detection — all existing patterns use fixed iteration limits rather than measuring whether fixes are trending toward resolution

The referenced scripts (build-verify.sh, diff-gate.sh, merge-gate.py, worktree-setup.sh, worktree-cleanup.sh) are specified in SKILL.md files but may not all be implemented yet — need to verify existence before depending on them
